Vide this common order, abovementioned three appeals are being decided.
For convenience, the facts are being drawn from RFA-- 1450-1998.

2. By way of present appeal, challenge has been laid to an award dated 19.11.1992 19.11. passed by the Reference Court Court-cum-Addl.
Addl.

District Judge, Ropar whereby, petition under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') filed at the instance of respondent respondent-landowner(s)
seeking king enhancement of compensation against their acquired land was partly allowed.

3. Briefly stating, vide notification dated 03.03.1988 issued under Section 4 of o the Act followed by State Of Punjab vs Jarnail Singh on 8 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87106684/
1 notification dated 26.03.1988 RFA-1450-1998, RFA-1451-1998 and RFA- 2682-1998 -2- issued under Section 6 thereof, land belonging to the appellants, situated within the revenue estate of village Dargah Shah Khalid Bin Walid was acquired for public purpose i.e. for construction of Upper Branch Canal.

Award under Section 11 of the Act was passed by the Land Acquisition Collector on 28.03.1989, evaluating the acquired land in the following manner:-
 Barani Rs.26,000/- per acre  Gair Mumkin/Banjar Rs.22,000/- per acre  4.
Aggrieved thereof, respondents-landowners sough enhancement while invoking Section 18 of the Act.

Upon consideration, the Reference Court vide award dated 19.11.1992 made the following determination qua the acquired land:-
 Barani Land Rs.75,000/- per acre  Gair Mumkin/Banjar Land Rs.60,000/- per acre
In addition, respondents-landowners were awarded other statutory benefits/interest as well.
5. Aggrieved of the award dated 19.11.1982 passed by the Reference Court, the present appeals were filed.

6. Assailing the impugned award, learned counsel for the appellants submits that the evidence relied upon by the appellants in the shape of Ex.R-2 i.e. Aks Shijra giving the location of the land in question as compared to the acquired land belonging to the village Dargah Shah Khalid Bin Walid was ignored by the Reference Court without recording any reasons therein.

He further submits that the assessment of compensation was made merely on the basis of RFA-1450-1998, RFA-1451-1998 and RFA- 2682-1998 -3- guess work, without relying upon any piece of evidence led by the parties and thus, the enhancement awarded vide impugned award was unsustainable in law.
7.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents while relying upon decision passed by this Court in RFA-2475-1987 dated 31.08.1989 submits that with respect to the land situated within District Ropar, a compromise was arrived at between the then Chief Minister and the Members of the Action Committee representing the landowners, wherein, it was settled that against the acquisition of land for Satluj-Yamuna link canal, compensation @1,00,000/- per acre for chahi land be awarded besides other benefits to the landowners and based thereupon, the following enhancement was made in favour of the landowners:-

sentences.text: I have heard learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the records.
The land in question belongs to Village Dargah Shah Khalid Bin Walid, the then Tehsil Ropar, District Patiala.

The Land Acquisition Collector vide its award dated 28.03.1989 determined the compensation @
Rs.26,000/- per acre for Barani whereas qua Gair Mumkin/Banjar it was assessed @ Rs.22,000/-
per acre which came to be enhanced to Rs.75,000/- per acre for Barani and Rs.62,000/- per acre for Gair Mumkin/Banjar land vide Reference Court award dated RFA-1450-1998, RFA-1451-1998 and RFA- 2682-1998 -4- 19.11.1992.

The relevant observations made by this Court in its judgment dated 31.08.1989 passed in RFA-2475-1987 relating to the land belonging to District Ropar based on the settlement between the then Chief Minister, Punjab and the Members of the Action Committee representing the landowners, thus, can easily be relied upon for the purposes of adjudication of case in hand as well to justify the enhancement awarded by the Reference Court in favour of landowners/respondents herein.

Relevant portion from the aforementioned judgment are reproduced hereunder:-
4. "....... The Chief Minister arrived at a settlement with the members of the Action Committee.

This settlement although was between the members of the Action Committee who principally belonged to District Ropar and the Chief Minister, Punjab yet it does furnish a good instance for determining the market value of the acquired land.

Under the settlement, the Chahi land had to be evaluated at the rate of Rs.
1,00,000/- per acre.

In addition thereto other benefits were also given to the claimants, namely, a member of the claimant's family was to be given a Government job or job in any public sector undertaking, plots were to be offered at the reserve price at Mohali or at other urban estates.

The settlement may not attain the character of a binding contract since it was not entered into as provided under Article 299 of the Constitution of India and may not be construed as a contract in terms thereof but nevertheless it is a piece of evidence which could be taken into consideration for determining the market value.
5. The settlement is a post notification transaction.
All transactions which are relevant fairly afford a criterion of the value of the property on the date of notification.
Post notification transactions cannot be ignored altogether.

In the instant case, as observed, earlier, the settlement was arrived at between the head of the Government and the representatives of the claimants regarding fixation of the market value and cannot be ignored.
The Appellate Court can take note of subsequent event when its correctness is not disputed.
6. Under the settlement, the Chahi land has to be evaluated at a price not less than Rs. 1,00,000 per acre.
The land situated in Powal is within the Periphery Control Act and has higher potentiality than other land
Under the circumstances, it will be just and fair if the Chahi land is evaluated at Rs.1,25,000/-per acre.

7. The classification of the land made by the Collector and the Acquisition Court cannot be ignored and no meaningful argument was addressed by either of RFA-1450-1998, RFA-1451-1998 and RFA- 2682-1998 -5- State Of Punjab vs Jarnail Singh on 8 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87106684/

sentences.text: 3 the parties to dislodge the finding recorded by the Land Acquisition Court regarding classification of the land.

8. The value of the Barani land which is obviously inferior to the Chahi land is assessed at Rs.
75,000/- and the Banjar land is valued at Rs. 55,000, - per acre."

9. Accordingly, in the aforementioned facts and circumstances, the enhancement awarded in favour of respondents-landowners being in consonance with the market value as well as the consent accorded by the then Chief Minsiter, Punjab in case of land acquired in District Ropar and the same even been upheld by this Court, finding no illegality or perversity, the present appeals are dismissed and the award dated 19.11.1982 passed the Land Acquisition Collector
is thus, upheld.
